label: Fighter Strength & Power - Four-Week Base
summary: Build relative strength and explosive capacity around fight practice, with focused chest, calf and arm development.
outcomes: Develop chest, calves and biceps alongside fight training
Keep course-led bag practice flexible and easy to record

equipment: Barbell, weight plates and squat rack
Clear turf or floor space for low-volume jumps and slams
Heavy bag and normal boxing equipment

description:
Four weeks of strength-led preparation around striking, grappling and technical bag practice. Two main lifting sessions and a shorter Saturday session include focused chest, calf and biceps work.

Start with the shown two-set base and leave 3-4 clean reps available. In weeks 2-3, add a third set only where marked if recovery allows; leave about three reps available. Rest fully, keep power crisp and add load only after cleanly reaching the top of the rep range.

In week 4, hold the recovered week-3 dose or return to the two-set base when tired. Review after four weeks from your start; no automatic phase change. Keep lifting days within 90 min, Sunday optional and record chosen classes and course lessons.

days.label: Monday - MMA striking class
days.focus: Attend the scheduled class. Log duration, drills, pads and sparring as performed; build consistency without treating every live round as maximal.

days.label: Tuesday - Strength A
days.focus: Squat, upper chest and vertical pull; 90-min cap. Two-set base. Weeks 2-3: add a third set to power, squat, incline press, pulldown and standing calves only if recovered.

items.name: Easy cardio, dynamic preparation and lift warm-up sets
items.dose: 10 min total: 2 min easy bike, 3 min dynamic ankle/hip/shoulder movement, 5 min gradual preparation sets. Count lift preparation within this allowance.
items.cue: Prepare the movements you will train without turning the warm-up into conditioning.

items.name: Countermovement Jump

prescription.note: Rest 90s. Reset each rep; stop before speed or landing quality drops. Weeks 2-3: add a third set if recovered.

items.cue: Use a clear, permitted area. Jump from the floor, land quietly and reset; crisp repetitions train rapid force production without a box. Skip if there is no safe space.

items.name: Barbell Back Squat

prescription.note: Rest 150-180s. First session: try 60-65 kg total only if warm-up sets feel easy; adjust down as needed. Weeks 2-3: add a third set if recovered.

items.cue: Use a repeatable comfortable depth and a controlled descent. Drive up with intent; keeping clean reps in reserve supports strength work alongside classes.

items.name: Incline Barbell Bench Press

prescription.note: Rest 120-180s. First session: try 40 kg total if comfortable; no forced repetitions. Weeks 2-3: add a third set if recovered.

items.cue: Use a comfortable low-to-moderate incline and controlled lowering. Stable pressing gives a repeatable upper-chest stimulus.

items.name: Plate-Loaded Lat Pulldown

prescription.note: Rest 120s. Weeks 2-3: add a third set if recovered.

items.cue: Pull without swinging and control the return. This is the loadable vertical-pull strength anchor without needing a dip belt.

items.name: Standing Calf Raise Machine

prescription.note: Rest 60-90s. Weeks 2-3: add a third set if recovered.

items.cue: Keep knees softly straight, lower under control and pause briefly at the bottom without bouncing. Progress load only while preserving the same ankle range.

items.name: Standing Dumbbell Curl
items.cue: Keep the upper arms steady and control the descent; direct elbow-flexion work gives the biceps a consistent growth stimulus.

items.name: Dead Bug
items.cue: Exhale and extend only as far as you can without arching; this trains trunk control without adding heavy spinal loading.

items.name: Easy upright bike
items.cue: Keep a full-sentence conversational pace. Omit after an unusually demanding class or if it would exceed 90 min; record the change in notes.

items.name: Easy walk and comfortable mobility
items.dose: 5 min: easy walking, relaxed breathing and comfortable calf, hip and chest mobility.
items.cue: Let breathing settle; stretch gently without forcing range.

days.label: Wednesday - Grappling or conditioning class
days.focus: Choose ONE scheduled class. Log which class, duration, live rounds and perceived difficulty. A hard class counts toward the week's conditioning; do not add extra finishers.

days.label: Thursday - Strength B
days.focus: Hip extension, single-leg strength, rowing and shoulder support; 90-min cap. Weeks 2-3: add a third set to slams and rows only if recovered.

items.name: Easy cardio, dynamic preparation and lift warm-up sets
items.dose: 10 min total: 2 min easy bike, 3 min dynamic ankle/hip/shoulder movement, 5 min gradual preparation sets. Count lift preparation within this allowance.
items.cue: Prepare the movements you will train without turning the warm-up into conditioning.

items.name: Overhead Slam-Ball Slam

prescription.note: Rest 90s. Reset each rep; stop before speed or landing quality drops. Weeks 2-3: add a third set if recovered.

items.cue: Use a light, non-bouncing slam ball in a clear permitted area. Reset before each fast slam; stop when output slows. No wall throws or heavy grinding.

items.name: Single-Leg Glute Kickback Machine
items.cue: Keep the pelvis stable and move through the hip rather than arching the lower back. This supplies direct hip-extension work without deadlifts.

items.name: Dumbbell Split Squat (rear foot on floor)
items.cue: Use a stable stance and controlled depth. Single-leg loading develops force and balance without needing a box or rear-foot elevation.

items.name: Plate-Loaded Seated Row

prescription.note: Rest 120s. Weeks 2-3: add a third set if recovered.

items.cue: Keep the torso still and let the shoulders move comfortably; a controlled row balances the week's pressing and striking.

blocks.label: Chest, calves and rear shoulders - about 17 min

items.name: Chest Press Machine
items.cue: Use a comfortable grip and controlled range. This adds chest volume with a stable setup after the main work.

items.name: Seated Calf Raise
items.cue: Move through a consistent ankle range without bouncing. Select the load for clean repetitions, not for the machine's displayed number.

items.name: Rear-Delt Machine
items.cue: Keep the chest supported and move without shrugging. This adds light rear-shoulder work alongside the week's pressing.

items.name: Standing Cable Pallof Press
items.cue: Stand side-on to the cable and resist turning as you press out; use a light load that lets the trunk stay still.

items.name: Easy upright bike
items.cue: Keep a full-sentence conversational pace. Omit after an unusually demanding class or if it would exceed 90 min; record the change in notes.

items.name: Easy walk and comfortable mobility
items.dose: 5 min: easy walking, relaxed breathing and comfortable calf, hip and chest mobility.
items.cue: Let breathing settle; stretch gently without forcing range.

days.label: Friday - Course-led bag practice
days.focus: 10-min shadowboxing/footwork warm-up; chosen Varga or Jeff Chan lesson, usually 6-8 x 2-3 min with 60s rest; 5-min cooldown. Log the actual lesson and rounds. Technical quality leads; 90 min is a ceiling, not a duration to fill.

days.label: Saturday - Strength C and technical bag
days.focus: Shorter full-body lifting, chest/calves/biceps and chosen technical bag lesson. About 40 min lifting; stay within 90 min total.

items.name: Easy cardio, dynamic preparation and lift warm-up sets
items.dose: 10 min total: 2 min easy bike, 3 min dynamic ankle/hip/shoulder movement, 5 min gradual preparation sets. Count lift preparation within this allowance.
items.cue: Prepare the movements you will train without turning the warm-up into conditioning.

blocks.label: Full-body strength and accessories - about 40 min

items.name: Leg Press Machine
items.cue: Use a controlled depth without the pelvis rolling off the pad. Keep this a moderate third leg exposure rather than another heavy squat day.

items.name: Incline Dumbbell Bench Press
items.cue: Use a comfortable incline and controlled lowering. This is the second weekly incline exposure for upper-chest development.

items.name: Strict Bodyweight Pull-Up
items.cue: Use strict repetitions and stop with at least three clean reps available. Practise the movement; do not chase a max-repetition test. No improvised dumbbell loading.

items.name: Shoulder Press Machine
items.cue: Use a comfortable path without arching. A small vertical-press dose completes the week's pushing patterns.

items.name: Leg Curl Machine
items.cue: Keep the hips supported and control the return. This complements hip-extension work with direct hamstring knee-flexion loading.

items.name: Standing Calf Raise Machine
items.cue: Repeat Tuesday's controlled ankle range and avoid bouncing. Reduce load if it would change your footwork afterward.

items.name: Standing Dumbbell Curl
items.cue: Keep the elbows quiet and finish with clean reps available. The second direct arm exposure keeps the weekly dose manageable.

blocks.label: Chosen technical bag lesson - 17-31 min including rest

items.name: Course-led Technical Bag Rounds
perRound: R1: Practise a combination from the chosen lesson.
R2: Continue the lesson with balanced stance and footwork.
R3: Follow the selected lesson's next drill.
R4: Repeat the lesson's combinations with controlled execution.
R5: Keep the chosen technical focus; stop forcing speed.
R6: Finish with clean technique; record the lesson and any changes.
items.cue: Default: 6 x 2 min. Follow the actual course; up to 8 x 2 min or 6 x 3 min only while quality and the 90-min cap allow. Keep technical intent and record lesson, round length and actual rounds in notes.

items.name: Easy walk and comfortable mobility
items.dose: 5 min: easy walking, relaxed breathing and comfortable calf, hip and chest mobility.
items.cue: Let breathing settle; stretch gently without forcing range.

days.label: Sunday - Optional recovery or day off
days.focus: Rest by default. Optional easy mobility, sauna or cryotherapy if desired; record what you actually did. No requirement to add a workout or make up missed sessions.
